channel.title: Marketplace Morning Report
channel.description: Get up to speed on the news each morning with our daily radio show and podcast, “Marketplace Morning Report,” hosted by Kimberly Adams. We give you the economy without the anxiety, in the amount of time it takes to brew a cup of coffee. Start your day with us, on air or by downloading our podcast, for context and perspective on the economic news that matters to you.
channel.itunes:author: Marketplace

item.title: When celebrities are also salespeople
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
"For as long as there is stuff to sell, the way to sell stuff is by making famous people, influential people, sell it," says Bobby Finger, co-host of the pop culture podcast "Who? Weekly." Odds are, if you're hunting for Black Friday or Cyber Monday deals, you'll encounter some celebrity brands. This morning, we bring you a segment from "This Is Uncomfortable" that explores the rise of celebrity and influencer products. But first, how are international markets looking today?

item.title: Food banks are busy
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
This time of year is always busy for food banks. Lots of people come in wanting to donate and volunteer, and lots more come needing assistance. But throughout this year, food banks and pantries have been noticing a significant increase in demand — largely because of inflation and recent cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program. We hear more. Also: a check on international markets and understanding why it matters who heads the Government Accountability Office.

item.title: A look at who's not receiving VC funding
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
Venture capital is a market that has grown to something like $500 billion. But the vast majority of that money is not going to VC funds led by women. This morning, we bring you a snippet from the Aspen Institute’s WIN Summit panel titled “Smart Money: Investing in Women," which brought together leaders in business, academia, and more to highlight solutions and ideas that help women thrive in the economy. Also in this episode: digging into GDP growth and hearing what it's like to juggle school and a new child.

item.title: If you give a radio host a crossbow
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
People dish up all sorts of Thanksgiving classics: turkey and stuffing; pumpkin or sweet potato pie; maybe even a casserole. And perhaps there's something specific to your family or culture. Wild game is often on the menu for the family of "Marketplace Morning Report" host Kimberly Adams. This year, Kimberly’s Uncle David taught her some hunting skills. Today, we follow along that journey. But first, how can shoppers make sure they get the best Black Friday deal?

item.title: A new round of Trump tariffs
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
President Donald Trump is reportedly getting ready to announce more tariffs. The Trump administration is targeting China, the European Union, and more than a dozen other countries it says are flooding the U.S. with subsidized, cheap imports. We dig into why the administration is considering more tariffs — and why now. Also in this podcast: Interest rates haven't tamped down price increases, and a Portland newsletter writer tracks grocery prices for locals.

item.title: Can Dollar Tree become a one-stop shop?
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
Dollar Tree reported strong quarterly earnings this week. On its earnings call, the discount retailer said that a wider range of items on its shelves is letting customers get more of their shopping done in a single trip. Then, as part of a conversation from "Smart Money: Investing in Women" at the Aspen Institute's WIN Summit in New York City, we hear what accessing capital and launching a business look like in the age of AI. And later, what are businesses doing with all of those tariff refunds?
